run.question: We're getting mapping errors and slow indexing on our events index. Can you check the field mappings for our app-188-index-* indexes and tell me if any have an unusually high number of fields? What's the exact field count for each?

report.summary: All four indices matching app-188-index-* exist and are green/open at query time (2026-11-23T17:41:37Z–17:41:44Z, the tool has no time range). app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b and app-188-index-c each have exactly 10 top-level mapped properties and no multi-fields. app-188-index-x is the outlier: 523 top-level properties, or 655 fields when its 132 keyword multi-fields are counted — roughly 52x the others. Index-x's fields are machine-generated families (counter_0001…counter_0519, flag_0002…flag_0518, label_0003…label_0519, metric_0000…metric_0516) plus only @timestamp, event_type and user_id, and it holds 1 document in 204.4kb while a/b/c hold 0 documents in 227b each. Index-x's schema also differs from a/b/c, which share action, duration_ms, error_message, event_type, ip_address, metadata, session_id, status, user_id. That field explosion in app-188-index-x is the strongest candidate explanation for mapping errors and slow indexing, but I did not observe the error messages or indexing-latency measurements themselves, so the causal link remains a hypothesis.

claims.text: The pattern app-188-index-* matches exactly four indices, all status open and health green at query time: app-188-index-a (docs.count 0, 227b), app-188-index-b (0, 227b), app-188-index-c (0, 227b) and app-188-index-x (1, 204.4kb).

app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b and app-188-index-c each have exactly 10 top-level mapped properties and 0 keyword multi-fields (total 10 fields each); the three mappings list the same property set: @timestamp (date), action (keyword), duration_ms (integer), error_message (text), event_type (keyword), ip_address (ip), metadata (object), session_id (value redacted by the tool), status (keyword), user_id (keyword).
app-188-index-x has 523 top-level mapped properties and 655 fields counted with its 132 keyword sub-fields (multi-fields), versus 10 properties each for app-188-index-a, -b and -c.
In app-188-index-x the 523 top-level properties break down by type as 131 long, 132 text, 130 boolean, 129 float and 1 date.

The app-188-index-x mapping consists mainly of generated field-name families — counter_0001 through counter_0519 (long), flag_0002 through flag_0518 (boolean), label_0003 through label_0519 (text with keyword sub-field) and metric_0000 through metric_0516 (float) — alongside @timestamp (date), event_type (text with keyword sub-field) and user_id (text with keyword sub-field).
app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b and app-188-index-c are not affected by field growth: each shows 10 top-level properties and no multi-fields, i.e. no unusually high field count.

The field explosion in app-188-index-x (523 properties / 655 fields from generated counter_/flag_/label_/metric_ names, with only 1 document stored) is the likely source of the reported mapping errors and slow indexing on that index; this is inferred from the mapping shape only and was not verified against an error message or an indexing-latency measurement.

app-188-index-x uses a different document schema than its siblings: it lacks action, duration_ms, error_message, ip_address, metadata, status and session_id that a/b/c share, and maps event_type as text+keyword instead of keyword; a schema or index-template mismatch is therefore a second candidate cause of mapping errors on this index, unverified.

gaps: I did not observe any actual mapping-error message or indexing-latency measurement for app-188-index-x; no Elasticsearch error log or index/search latency signal was queried, so the causal link between the 523-field mapping and the reported symptoms is unverified.

Index settings were not observed (for example index.mapping.total_fields.limit, dynamic mapping mode, index templates), so I cannot state which limit or template produced the wide mapping or whether writes are currently rejected.

The mappings view has no time range: it reflects the indices at 2026-11-23T17:41:37Z–17:41:44Z only, not during the earlier part of the authorized window, so when the counter_/flag_/label_/metric_ fields were created is unknown.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so I could not check what introduced the generated field names into app-188-index-x.
session_id in the a/b/c mappings had its value redacted by the tool, so its type could not be verified.
No application logs for the writer of these indices were identified or read, so the producer-side cause (for example a document with per-metric generated keys) is unchecked.
next_steps: Confirm the reported errors by inspecting Elasticsearch logs for mapper_parsing_exception / illegal_argument_exception messages naming app-188-index-x and its field paths.
Compare index.mapping.total_fields.limit and any index template applied to app-188-index-* so the writer for index-x can be matched to the a/b/c schema.

If the generated counter_/flag_/label_/metric_ fields are not needed for search, plan a reindex of app-188-index-x into a mapping that keeps the a/b/c schema and stores the wide payload as a single flattened or disabled field.

query.jq: to_entries | map({index: .key, props: (.value.mappings.properties | keys | length), with_keyword_multifield: ([.value.mappings.properties[] | select(.fields.keyword != null)] | length), total_including_multifields: ((.value.mappings.properties | keys | length) + ([.value.mappings.properties[] | select(.fields.keyword != null)] | length))})
